pages.html:
TomaTío manual

TomaTío turns a WordPress site into a private brain for your team's AI agents. This manual describes TomaTío 1.9.10.

In wp-admin, a path such as TomaTío > Connect an AI means the Connect an AI tab under the TomaTío menu.

Start here

  • What a brain does
  • How TomaTío compares: starting on your computer, the three ways to move a brain, and where others are ahead.
  • Install on your own computer: try TomaTío on your Mac with one command, and move it to a server later.

For the person who runs the server

  • Install TomaTío
  • Settings and admin screens
  • Export, import, migration and backups

For the people on the team

  • Connect an AI
  • Agents, people and scopes
  • Memory
  • Knowledge and procedures
  • The Review Queue
  • Documents written together
  • HTML pages
  • Artifact settings: every setting of a document or page, its default and who may change it.
  • Sharing pages and documents
  • TíoDay: your day, kept current by your AIs.
  • Delegated authority and role switching

For the AIs connected to a brain

  • For AIs connected to a brain

Words used here

Word Means
Brain One WordPress site running TomaTío.
Agent The account an AI signs in as.
Tío A person's own agent.
Scope A shared space. Agents read and write by scope.
Curator A person who approves knowledge and manages the brain.
Member Any other person with an account.
Artifact A document or an HTML page.
Lead The agent in charge of one artifact.
Members address An artifact's permanent address for signed-in people.
Share link An address that opens an artifact for people outside the brain.
Handoff An agent asking a person to review work.
Model Context Protocol (MCP) How AI apps connect to the brain.
Portable Context Protocol (PCP) The open format of exports.

pages.name: what-is-tomatio
pages.title: What a TomaTío brain does
pages.html:
What a TomaTío brain does

This page explains what a brain holds and who does what in it.

TomaTío is a WordPress plugin that turns a WordPress site into a brain: one shared memory for your team's AI agents, on your own server. AI apps such as Claude and ChatGPT connect to it over the Model Context Protocol (MCP).

What is in a brain

  • Memory: notes agents save while they work.
  • Knowledge: official facts. Agents suggest them; people approve them.
  • Procedures: official playbooks, written by people.
  • Artifacts: documents that agents write together, and small HTML pages and apps.
  • Handoffs: an agent asking a person to review work.
  • Audit log: a record of every action and who did it.

Who is who

  • Agents are the accounts AIs sign in as. A person's own agent is their Tío.
  • Curators approve knowledge and manage the brain. Administrators can also export and import.
  • Members are everyone else with an account.
  • Scopes are shared spaces. An agent reads and writes only in its own scopes.

See Agents, people and scopes.

The rules

  1. Agents only see their scopes.
  2. A fact becomes official only when a curator approves it, or, if a curator switches this on, automatically for facts from curators' own Tíos. See The Review Queue.
  3. Every action is logged, with the agent and the person it acted for.
  4. If you connect your AI as yourself, its work is credited to one of your agents, with your name beside it. See Delegated authority and role switching.
  5. A full export in the open Portable Context Protocol (PCP) format takes everything with you. See Export, import, migration and backups.

The brain runs no AI model and collects no analytics. Apart from an update check, it contacts no outside service unless you switch one on. Give it a WordPress install of its own: see Install TomaTío.

Every feature is free, under the GNU General Public License (GPL). TomaTío is an open-source project by Roger Gentry and Dennis Kittrell.

pages.name: connect-an-ai
pages.title: Connect an AI
pages.html:
Connect an AI

This page shows how to connect an artificial intelligence (AI) app, such as Claude, ChatGPT or Cursor, to a brain, and how to manage the connection. It describes TomaTío 1.9.10.

The connector address

AI apps connect over the Model Context Protocol (MCP), at the brain's connector address:

https://<your-site>/wp-json/agent-brain/v1/mcp

There is also a role-switching address ending in /mcp-roles, where you connect as yourself and the AI switches between your agents. See Delegated authority and role switching.

Curators and administrators can copy both on TomaTío > Agents > Connect an AI, which also has steps for each app. On a site used only for TomaTío, the home page shows them too.

Claude (claude.ai and Claude Desktop)

  1. In claude.ai, open Customize > Connectors, click Add and choose Custom connector. In Claude Desktop, open Settings > Connectors.
  2. Name it, for example "Example brain", and paste the connector address.
  3. Click Connect, sign in to the brain if asked, and finish on the consent screen.
  4. Claude starts every tool on Needs approval. In the connector's settings, set Read-only tools and Write/delete tools to Always allow. Then set these back to Needs approval: Archive a page or document; Make a page or document private again; Turn off a share link; Delete a record from a page's data; Delete a file from a page; Change a page's files; Bring back an earlier version; Bring back an earlier version of a record. Set Set the rules for a page's data to Blocked.

Claude Code

Claude Code signs in as one agent with a WordPress application password. There is no consent screen, and it never switches roles.

  1. On Connect an AI, under Agents to sign in as, click Application password next to the agent and create one. It is shown only once.
  2. Encode it with the agent's login: printf 'agent-login:xxxx xxxx xxxx xxxx xxxx xxxx' | base64
  3. Under Claude Code > Show the steps, copy the command and replace BASE64 with the result.

Other apps

In ChatGPT (developer mode), Cursor, VS Code (GitHub Copilot), Gemini CLI, OpenAI Codex or Windsurf, add an MCP server at the connector address with the Streamable HTTP (Hypertext Transfer Protocol) transport. The app finds the sign-in itself, and you approve it on the consent screen. Apps that cannot, such as Zed, use an application password in an Authorization: Basic header, as above.

The consent screen

It names the app and who you are signed in as. Not you? lets you sign in as someone else.

  • Curators and administrators choose who the AI works as, under Connect as: an active agent, or Me. Your default agent, or else one you issued, is marked Recommended. With Me, the AI reads with your access and saves as your default agent.
  • Everyone else, and everyone on the role-switching address, sees what the AI will be able to do. Members get no tools. See Agents, people and scopes.
  • If the brain allows it, an unticked box offers Let this AI act with my rights when I ask. See Delegated authority and role switching.

Click Allow access. The sign-in renews itself while you use the app, and expires after 30 days without use.

See and revoke connections

  • Connect an AI > Your connections lists the apps connected as you, with their status.
  • On your profile, MCP Agent Authorizations lists the connections you allowed. Click Revoke to sign one out.
  • TomaTío > Agents > Connected apps shows curators every connected app.

Every request is in the audit log.

After an update

An app keeps the tool list it got when it connected. When an update changes the tools, Your connections says "Update available — reconnect to refresh the tool list". Remove the connector and add it again (in Claude Code, claude mcp remove <name> first), then set Claude's tool permissions again.

A connected AI should start with Start here: what this brain knows. See For AIs connected to a brain.

pages.name: agents-and-scopes
pages.title: Agents, people and scopes
pages.html:
Agents, people and scopes

This page explains who can do what in a brain: the roles, the agents that artificial intelligence (AI) apps sign in as, and the scopes that limit what each can read and write. It describes TomaTío 1.9.10.

Roles

Role Can
Agent Use the brain's tools from an AI app, within its scopes. It can never approve knowledge, grant scopes, publish or manage the brain.
Curator All of that, plus approve knowledge, grant scopes, publish, see the audit log and manage the brain.
Administrator All a curator can, plus WordPress itself and Export and import.

Everyone else, such as Subscribers, is a member. Members open what is shared with them (see Sharing) but cannot use the brain's tools. To let a member's AI work in the brain, make an agent for it.

Agents

An agent is a WordPress account with the Agent role. Each gets an agent ID (identifier) such as designer-027fd774.agnt.example.com.

To add one, do one of these:

  • In WordPress, under Users, add a user with the Agent role, then give it scopes.
  • On TomaTío > Agents, click Create agent registration and give the AI the key. The key is shown once and expires within 24 hours.
  • On a role-switching connection, ask your AI to propose one. You approve it in the Review Queue within 24 hours.

An observer agent is set up to read only. The other classes (executor, contributor, lead) are labels.

On TomaTío > Agents, each agent has Suspend, Reactivate, Revoke (final) and Revoke app passwords. Grant approval lets an agent approve other agents' document sections and assemble documents in the scopes it can write; it does not make it a curator. Agent View shows the brain exactly as one agent sees it.

Scopes

A scope is a shared space. Every memory, knowledge entry, procedure, page and document belongs to one.

Each agent has scopes it may read and scopes it may write. It only finds what is in its read scopes, and writes elsewhere are refused. An agent with no scopes sees nothing.

A new brain starts with one scope named after the site, such as "Example team". Every curator and administrator can read and write it. While it is the only scope, new agents get it too.

Manage scopes

Curators and administrators use TomaTío > Agents > Scopes to add, rename and delete scopes, and to grant or revoke an agent's Read or Write access. A scope cannot be deleted while anything still belongs to it. You can also tick an agent's scopes under Agent Scopes on its profile. Every change is in the audit log.

These screens grant scopes to agents only. People read with their own scopes, and curators and administrators get the first scope automatically.

Who can work as which agent

On the consent screen, a curator or administrator can connect an AI as any active agent. With role switching, you can switch only into agents whose scopes are all within your own. See Delegated authority and role switching.

pages.name: export-and-migration
pages.title: Export, import, migration and backups
pages.html:
Export, import, migration and backups

This page is for administrators. It explains how to take a brain's data out of TomaTío 1.9.10, bring it into another brain, and back it up. Everything except backups is on TomaTío > Export and import: export and import side by side at the top, the other flows in their own boxes below, and the long explanations under About this page.

To do this Use
Move the whole site to another server, at the same address Your host's migration tool or a WordPress migration plugin: see Move the whole site
Get one file with the whole brain Export
Move a whole brain to a new, empty brain, such as from your computer to a server Migrate a brain here
Bring some scopes of another brain into this one Move scopes here
Add pages from another brain or tool, for review Import an archive

Three ways to move context

  • The whole brain. Move the WordPress site, TomaTío included, to another server, or migrate the brain from one archive into a new, empty brain.
  • Everything in it. A full export is one archive in the open Portable Context Protocol (PCP) format, which another brain or any PCP tool can read.
  • Any part of it. Every export holds the whole brain. To move only part of it, choose scopes (Move scopes here) or bring pages in for review (Import an archive) on the brain that receives it.

Move the whole site

To move a brain to another server and keep its address, move the WordPress site as you would any other: with your host's migration tool, a migration plugin, or a copy of its files and database. Everything comes along, including passwords, agent keys, AI connections and share links, because only the server changes.

Keep AUTH_KEY and AUTH_SALT in wp-config.php as they are (migration tools copy them), and AGENT_BRAIN_SECRET_KEY if you set one. TomaTío seals stored keys and share links with them; with new values, those stop working.

A brain on your own computer runs on SQLite, so it moves to a server with an export and Migrate a brain here instead. See Install on your own computer.

Export

Under Take everything with you, click Make a full export. You get one zip file in the open Portable Context Protocol (PCP) v0.3 format, signed with this brain's own key.

It holds the whole brain: memories, knowledge and procedures with their history, people, agents and scopes, house rules, documents and pages with their data and files, review requests, the audit log and forget receipts. It never holds passwords, keys, connection tokens, share-link tokens or settings. Every export holds the whole brain; to move part of it, choose what to bring in on the receiving brain.

An export is not encrypted. Keep it as carefully as the brain itself.

The archive is kept on the server for 24 hours by default (1 hour to 7 days, in Kept archives), so download it right away. Forget deletes every kept archive. If the server has no private folder for archives, the button reads Export and download and nothing is kept. A server admin can set one with AGENT_BRAIN_EXPORT_DIR in wp-config.php.

A big brain can take longer than a web request allows. Export it with WP-CLI (the WordPress command line) instead:

wp tomatio export --output=/secure/place/brain.pcp.zip

Migrate a brain here

Use this to move a brain to a new server.

  1. Install TomaTío on a fresh WordPress site.
  2. Make a full export on the old brain and download it.
  3. On the new brain, open Migrate a brain here and choose the file.
  4. Under Bind me to this person of the archive, pick who you were in the old brain.
  5. Leave Dry run ticked and click Check or migrate. Nothing is written yet; read the report.
  6. Untick Dry run and run it again.

For a big archive, use wp tomatio migrate <file> --user=<admin> --dry-run, then run it without --dry-run.

The new brain must be empty: no memories, knowledge, procedures, documents, pages, review requests, house rules, forget receipts, or scopes other than the one a new brain starts with. User accounts may exist. The migration is all or nothing. You can leave chosen scopes, people or agents behind.

Passwords, keys and connections never come over, and old share links do not work at the new address. Every person and agent comes back unbound, so nobody can sign in yet. Two sections of the page fix that:

  • Principals: Bind and send link emails a person a link to set a password. Bind and make an application password gives an agent a new key, shown once.
  • Reconnect: Send invitations to everyone at once, Make keys and download them for all agents, make share links again (Make a new link or Not needed), and free names claimed on shared pages (Release the name).

Then add every AI (artificial intelligence) connector again at the new address, as in Connect an AI.

Move scopes here

Use this to bring a project from another brain into this one while it is in use. Choose the scopes to move from the other brain's export. Their people and agents come too, as unbound accounts unless you match them to accounts here.

Everything waits for a person: pages go to the Review Queue, approved document sections go back to waiting for review, and no page version is live until someone approves it, unless you tick Keep approved what the source had approved. Share links are never brought over. Do a dry run first.

Import an archive

Use Bring pages in to add pages from another brain or another PCP tool: drop the archive on the box or choose it. They arrive as proposals in the Review Queue. Scopes, people and access here do not change. Documents, HTML (HyperText Markup Language) pages and earlier versions stay behind.

Under Options, choose a scope for the pages (import never creates one), and what to do when a page's path is taken: keep both, skip, or replace. Do a dry run first. Importing the same archive again skips what came in before. For an archive bigger than the server's upload limit, use wp tomatio import.

Signatures

When an archive this brain made comes back, one changed after export is refused. An archive from another brain cannot be checked, so it is accepted with a note that its origin cannot be verified.

Backups

Backups are in TomaTío > Settings > Backups. They need the optional TomaTío Cloud service, connected in the Summarising section.

  • Turn on Back up every day and click Save, or click Back up now.
  • Backups are encrypted on your site before they are sent. Click Generate and download backup key (later Download backup key) and keep the key safe: the cloud never has a copy.
  • When a Forget completes, older backups are deleted and a new one starts.

There is no way to restore a backup yet: no button and no command. To be able to rebuild a brain, keep a recent full export somewhere safe.

Forget and uninstall

To remove a person's or a subject's data, see Memory. For what uninstalling removes, see Install.
